prompt.context: A large oil company with nation-wide retail petrol stations wishes to evaluate the competitiveness of its outlets.
prompt.question: What would you want to look at, how would you look, and what would you hope to find out?

framework: Understand what drives customer preferences — both subjectively (market research/surveys) and empirically (data from comparable stations)
Use the 4 Ps framework (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) to structure the content analysis of competitiveness
Assess both content issues (what to look at) and process issues (how to gather the required information)
Evaluate brand loyalty and switching costs — does owning good locations matter more than in-store competitiveness?

questions.prompt: How would you empirically compare performance across stations?
questions.guidance: If the client has enough stations, identify peer groups of stations in similar situations (similar traffic flows, population density, competitive environment). Compare how differences in format, pricing, and services affect volumes across these peer groups. Where good peer groups are unavailable, pilot changes at specific stations to isolate the effect of individual variables. Discuss how to design reliable tests (control groups, sample size, duration).

questions.prompt: How would you gather subjective customer preference data?
questions.guidance: Conduct market research using surveys combined with demographic profiles. Key attributes to probe: price competitiveness, convenience store offering, quality of service, pay-at-the-pump capability, ease of entrance and exit, lighting, store design, ease of credit card payment. Compare findings against industry averages and competitor benchmarks.

questions.prompt: How does brand loyalty and location affect the competitiveness analysis?
questions.guidance: Examine whether good locations in a market are foreclosed to the client. If so, in-store competitiveness may be secondary. Assess customer switching costs — what benefits must the client offer to win volume from competitors? Consider whether loyalty programs or brand equity can overcome a location disadvantage.

brainstorming.prompt: Using the 4 Ps framework, what specific factors should the client examine to evaluate the competitiveness of its petrol stations?

categories.name: Product
ideas: Convenience store product range and quality

categories.name: Place
ideas: Traffic flow and accessibility of locations
Number of pumps and queue times

recommendation: Conduct a two-track analysis: empirical peer-group benchmarking across the station network and structured customer survey research to surface subjective preference drivers
Apply the 4 Ps framework to identify the specific gaps in product, price, place, and promotion that explain volume underperformance at lagging stations
risks: Good locations may already be foreclosed to competitors, making in-store improvements insufficient to win volume
Customer switching costs may be low, meaning price is the dominant driver and non-price improvements yield limited return
Pilot tests may be contaminated by external factors (local promotions, road works) if not carefully controlled
next_steps: Segment the station network into peer groups by location type and competitive context
Design and launch a customer survey with demographic profiling
Identify two or three pilot stations to test format, pricing, or service changes and measure volume impact
Benchmark results against industry averages and set prioritised investment recommendations
